This is the Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.1,10,00,000/ for the Death of one Bhargav T.S. in a road traffic accident dated 04.02.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, on 04.02.2021 at about 5.15 a.m., the deceased Bhargav T.S. after writing his final examination of 2nd year, who was student of Cardiac Care Technology of Jayadeva Hospital, Bangalore, was went along with his friend Sanjay Gowda, Hemantha, Harsh and the accused by name Mithun and Mr.Mithun had taken the car bearing Reg.No.KA03AG 1375 for rent/hire from the 2nd respondent, which is self driving car (Zoom car) and for a small trip for relaxation of mind, when they reached near Lakkavalli cross, Terikere town, Chikkamagaluru District, Karnataka, with a care and caution, in the meantime unknown animal came SCCH-24 across the road on seeing the same the driver of the car took right turn and the staring was jammed and driver lost his control and dashed it to nearby tree in a rash and negligent manner with high speed towards Bangalore to Shimoga/Gokarna, Shimoga District, the deceased was one of the Co passenger of the car bearing KA03AG 1375, who was sitting along with Sanjay Gowda and Harsha, in the backside of the car, as a result, the deceased Bhargav T.S. sustained grievous bleeding head injuries, spinal card of the neck and other part of the body and other copassengers also sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the car driver of the deceased and his friends took him to Govt., Hospital for first aid and then shifted to Max Hospital and next day the deceased was shifted to Jain Hospital, Bangalore, for higher treatment wherein he was under the treatment for about 16 days and died on 20.02.2021.
So far they have spent upto Rs.10,00,000/ SCCH-24 towards medicine, surgery, transportation, nourishment, death ceremony etc..

2 3. The petitioners further averred that, before the accident the deceased was hale and healthy, was a student of CCT and in the future days his income wound have been Rs.80,000/ to Rs.1,00,000/
per month in any specialty hospitals and if the deceased would have gone to in other country his salary wound be about Rs.2,50,000/ per month.
Prior to the accident the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/ p.m., by doing tuition at home, he was the clever and intelligent student of the college.
They have suffered irreparable loss, damages, untold misery and love and affection due to untimely death of the deceased.
The Terikere Town police have registered a case against the driver of the car under their Cr.No.33/2021, u/Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1st Respondent is the insurer and the 2nd Respondent is the RC owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to them.
SCCH-24 4. In response to the summons, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels, but the Respondent No.1 alone has filed written statement.

5. The Respondent No.1 insurance company in the written statement has denied all the allegations made by the petitioner as false, admitted issuance of policy but their liability is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of Section 134(c) of M.V. Act and denied the involvement of the insured vehicle in the alleged accident.

Further submitted that as per the averments of the petition as well as the police records on the date of accident, the deceased was traveling as a inmates of the insured car, however, the insured has taken the liability only policy,
hence the inmates of the car are not covered under the policy.

Further submitted that the respondent No.2 knowing fully well that the driver did not possess valid and effective driving license and vehicle was not having valid permit and FC but even then has SCCH-24 willfully entrusted the vehicle in breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed;
1 . Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Bhargav T.S.?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Bhargav T.S. was died on account of road traffic accident on 04.02.2021 at about 05.15 a.m., near Lakkavalli cross, Terikere town, Chikkamangaluru District,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bering Reg.No.KA03AG 1375?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4. What Order or Award?
7.

9. My findings to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1 : In the affirmative, Issue No.2 : In the affirmative, Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the Following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents and SCCH-24 Petitioner No.3 and 4 are the brothers of the deceased.
In this regard, the Petitioners to prove this relationship have examined first Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically deposed this relationship in her chiefexamination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship the Petitioners have also produced death certificate of deceased and notarized copy of the ration card of family of petitioners as per Exs.P.9 and P16.
There is no contrary to these documents from the respondents.
In the Ex.P9 death certificate of the deceased his parents names are mentioned and in Ex.P.16 family ration card names of the Petitioners and deceased are also mentioned with their relationship.
Further, these documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioner.
As such, there are no reasons to discard SCCH-24 the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents and Petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are the brother of the deceased Bhargav T.S..
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

11. ISSUE No.2: The Petitioners to prove that the accident was occurred due the actionable negligence on part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA03AG1375 have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.

The PW.1 has specifically deposed in her evidence that her son Bhargav T.S. after writing his final examination of 2 nd year,
who was student of Cardiac Care Technology of Jayadeva Hospital, Bangalore, was went along with his friend Sanjay Gowda, Hemantha, Harsh and the accused by name SCCH-24 Mithun and Mr.Mithun took the car bearing Reg.No.KA 03AG1375 for rent/hire from the 2nd respondent,
which is self driving car (Zoom car) for a small trip for relaxation of mind, when they reached near Lakkavalli cross, Terikere town, Chikkamagaluru District, Karnataka, with a care and caution, in the meantime unknown animal came across the road on seeing the same the driver of the car took right turn and the staring was jammed and driver lost his control and dashed to nearby tree in a rash and negligent manner with high speed towards Bangalore to Shimoga/Gokarna, Shimoga District, the deceased was one of the Copassenger of the car bearing KA03AG 1375, who was sitting along with Sanjay Gowda and Harsha, in the backside of the car, as a result his son Bhargav T.S. sustained grievous bleeding head injuries, spinal card of the neck and other part of the body and other co passengers also sustained grievous injuries and died on 20.02.2021.

sentences.text: Respondent SCCH-24 No.1 has denied the case of the petitioners as false and contended that the insured vehicle was not involved in the accident and as they issued liability only policy and hence they are not liable to pay compensation to the deceased as he was inmate of the insured car.
In support of said defence the Respondent No.1 have not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
In the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove the case of the petitioners with regard to alleged manner of accident.

12. Further, the documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR in Cr.No.0033/2021 of Tarikere Town Police Station, FIS, Inquest Mahazar, PM report, spot mahazar, chargesheet, photos in two pages, seizure mahzar as per Exs.P.1 to P.8 are all public documents which have got presumptive value under law.

sentences.text: Therefore, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PW.1.

The PM report produced as per Ex.P.4 clearly SCCH-24 shows that "Death is due to septicemia as a result of injury sustained to the cervical cord" sustained in the accident and on account of such injuries he succumbed.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of the PW.1 coupled with the Exs.P.1 to P.8, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the driver of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA03AG1375 driven it in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life and dashed to near by tree, result of which deceased Bhargav T.S sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries during the treatment.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No. 3:
The PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and their loving son.

They have pleaded that due to the accidental injuries their SCCH-24 son deceased Bhargav T.S. died during the treatment and PM was conducted and later the cremation of their deceased son was conducted.
This court while discussing the issue No.2 has come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending car.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation.
Monthly income 14.

According to the Petitioners the deceased was a student of Cardiac Care Technology and he was earning Rs.10,000/ per month by doing tuition at home and in the future days his income would be Rs.80,000/ per month.

In this regard the petitioners to prove the education qualification of the deceased and his employment have produced student ID, SSLC marks card, PUC marks, 1st year and 2nd year B.Sc Marks card and third year B.Sc tuition fee paid receipt as per Exs.P.12 to P.16 and P.18.

But, to substantiate that the deceased was SCCH-24 earning by tuition the Petitioner has not examined any witness and he has also not produced any documents like receipts or the bank statement to ascertain his income.
But from the said marks cards it is proved that the deceased was student of CCT and had completed 2 nd year.
Therefore, in absence of sufficient evidence to support his claim that he was earning monthly more than Rs.20,000/ the claim of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
At the time of accident the deceased was aged about 21 years as could be make out from Ex.P.13/SSLC Marks card of the deceased.
The accident took place in the year 2021.

Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased and also considering that he was to finish final year CCT and as he had a good qualification would be earning better and hence the monthly Sri.T.S.Gowramma vs The Branch Manager on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10162075/
5
notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.15,000/ per month.
As such, Petitioners are entitled for the following compensation: SCCH-24 Age of the deceased 15.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of SSLC marks card of the deceased as per Ex.P.12.
As per this document, his date of birth is 01.03.2000.
The accident was occurred on 04.02.2021.
As such his age was 21 years as on the date of his death.
Therefore, the age of the deceased is considered 21 years.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarala Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

entities.text: Sarala Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has parents and brothers.

In the crossexamination of PW.1 it is elicited that the petitioner No.3 is doing business of chats, the 2 nd petitioner is suffering from ill health and the 4th petitioner is working in company and married.
The PW.1 has not produced any documents to show that the 2nd petitioner is SCCH-24 suffering from ill health and hence it cannot be considered.
Further as the petitioners 3 and 4 being major brothers and admittedly earning and hence the petitioners 2 to 4 cannot be treated as dependents on the deceased.
Therefore, the mother/petitioner No.1 is only considered as dependent on the deceased.

It is relevant to note that as per the recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in special leave petition No. 25590/2014 between National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others and other connected petitions, even in case of the death of self employed and fixed salary also, the Dependants are entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the deceased is alive then definitely he would have got bright future and got sufficient earnings.
Therefore, in the present case since the deceased is less than 40 years age, 40% future prospects have to be added to his monthly income.
However, as the deceased is a bachelor, as per the Sarala Verma case,  of his income has to be SCCH-24 deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

If 40% income is added to his monthly income, it comes around Rs.21,000/ (Rs.15,000/ + Rs.6,000/) and if 50%
is deducted towards his living and personal expenses, balance comes to Rs.10,500/ (Rs.21,000/ 
Rs.10,500/).
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.22,68,000/ (Rs.10,500/ X 12 X 18 = Rs.22,68,000/).

ii) TRANSPORTATION, MEDICAL EXPENSES AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS TO ESTATE:
In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have pleaded and deposed that they have spent Rs.10,00,000/ towards medicine,
surgery, transportation, nourishment, death ceremony of their deceased son.
There is no document produced regarding transportation of dead body and funeral expenses but under said circumstances it is also difficult SCCH-24 to maintain documents.
However, looking into the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.20,000/ towards funeral and transportation expenses.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:

6

On perusal of the petition averments and the documents produced it is clear that the accident had occurred on 04.02.2021 and the deceased Bhargav T.S. was taken to Govt., Hospital for first aid and then shifted to Max Hospital and next day the deceased was shifted to Jain Hospital, Bangalore, wherein under the treatment for about 16 days and he succumbed to the injuries on the 20.02.2021.

PW.1 has produced death summary, laboratory reports, two photos of deceased,
reimbursement of medical expenses issued by Star health insurance (for Rs.5,05,025/) and four MRI Scans
and they are marked at Ex.P10, P11 and P19 to P21.

As per death summary, SCCH-24 the deceased Bhargav T.S. was admitted as an inpatient at Bhagavan Mahaveer Jain Hospital from 05.02.2021 and he expired on 20.02.2021, on diagnoses found Traumatic paralegia C5C6 burst fracture, Septic shock, Tracheostomy, corpectomy Fusion, Autonomic dysfunction due to cervical injury and underwent surgery for C6 Corpectomy C6C7 fusion under GA_intermittent cervical plexus block on 06.02.2021 Tracheostomy under GA on 16.02.2021.
No contrary evidence is lead by the respondent No.1 to disprove the medical documents.

In the crossexamination of PW.1 it is elicited that in the inpatient final bill Rs.5,50,025/ paid by the Star Health Insurance Company, in the same bill a sum of Rs.34,058/ was given as discount and they have only paid Rs.54,518/.
The petitioners have examined Mr.Doulath Ram L. Medical Records Department (MRD Assistant) at Bhagavan Jain Hospital as PW.2 and produced documents as per Exs.P22 to P26.
His evidence SCCH-24 shows that the deceased was admitted in their hospital and took treatment.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.54,518/ under the medical bills.
iii) LOSS TO THE ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
Out of this, he was getting 1/2 of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.
iv) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
The Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents and Petitioner No.3 and 4 are the brothers of the deceased.
They have lost their loving son and brother.
If he was alive he would taken care of them and given full love and affection to the Petitioners.
In Magma General Insurance SCCH-24 company Limited the Hon'ble Apex court has considered the compensation under head of loss of consortium.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex court in three judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.

sentences.text:
In Paragraph 53 to 65, dealt with three conventional heads and discussed about "Consortium" to be a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium, as Sri.T.S.Gowramma vs The Branch Manager on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10162075/
7
well as filial consortium.

The right to consortium would include the company, care,
help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
Filial Consortium - A child's society, affection and companionship given to a parent.
Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for compensation under the head of consortium.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled a sum of Rs.1,60,000/
(Rs.40,000/ each) under this head.
SCCH-24

As such, in total, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.25,22,518/
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

Liability:
16.
As discussed above, the Respondent No.1  insurer has failed to prove its defence as contended.
Under these circumstances, it is very clear that Respondents being the insurer and the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation.
However, as the Petitioners have proved the existence of policy and its validity as on the date of accident, the insurer Respondent No.1 has primary liability to satisfy the award.
The Petitioners have claimed an amount of Rs.1,10,00,000/, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.25,22,518/.
Therefore the Petition is liable to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.
SCCH-24 17. ISSUE No.4:

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for  Compensation of Rs.25,22,518/ (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Twenty Two Thousand Five Hundred and Eighteen only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
